session.description: The address of a conversation to append to, as sennit://session/{id}. Omit to create a new one.

title.description: One specific line naming the conversation. Required when creating; on an append, supply it only to change it.

summary.description: What was decided, tried and left open. THE TRANSCRIPT IS NOT SEARCHABLE: this, the title and the tags are the entire searchable surface of a conversation. Write it for someone deciding whether to open the conversation.

tags.description: Two to four specific tags, reused from the vault's existing vocabulary where they fit. Read sennit://vault for it.

messages.description: The turns to store, in order. On an append, only the new ones.

name.description: The client's name, for example claude-code.

models.description: The models that spoke in the conversation.

preservedTail.description: Message ids worth keeping verbatim beside the summary. An accelerator, never a replacement for the transcript.

durable.description: Write to the network before returning instead of on the ordinary schedule. Use at the end of a long conversation, not on every append: each forced write costs a whole storage block whatever it holds.

archived.description: Put the conversation away, so it stops appearing in ordinary listings.

id.description: Stable and unique within this conversation. It is what a preserved tail, a fork point and a memory's provenance all point at.

role.description: Who produced the turn. Use tool for a turn that is only a tool result, if your runtime models it that way; otherwise put the result part in the user turn that carried it.

parts.description: The content, in order. Never a flat string: a string cannot hold a tool call, a thinking block or an image, so a conversation stored that way degrades into a chat log.

created.description: When the turn happened, RFC 3339. For display; order comes from the sequence, never from the clock.

parent.description: The id of the turn this one replies to, so a conversation that branched keeps its shape.

meta.description: What the runtime knew about the turn.

agent.description: Which agent produced it, when several were involved.

skill.description: The skill this turn is attributable to, if any.

memoryRefs.description: Ids of the memories that were in context for this turn. A transcript replayed without them reproduces the words and not the conditions.

ext.description: Your runtime's own fields for this turn, carried through untouched and returned exactly as given. Put anything here that this schema does not name rather than dropping it.

type.description: text, reasoning, toolCall, toolResult, file or resourceLink. A type this vault does not know is stored rather than refused, so a part your runtime has that this list does not is still safe to send under its own name.

text.description: The prose, for a text part, or the thinking, for a reasoning part.

signature.description: The opaque attestation attached to a reasoning block, which must survive for the block to be replayable.

callId.description: REQUIRED on both a toolCall and the toolResult it produced, and the SAME value on each. It is the only thing that correlates them, no later reader can reconstruct it, and a call without one is refused rather than stored broken.

input.description: The arguments it was called with, as they were sent.

content.description: A tool result's own parts, so a tool that returned an image is stored as one. A result that was a plain string is one text part.

isError.description: True when the tool reported a failure.

mediaType.description: The media type of an attachment.

ref.description: Where an attachment's bytes are held. Hold them by reference: inline base64 is the largest single cause of transcript bloat, and a session record that inlines it stops being small enough to be worth having.

uri.description: The address another record is at, for a resourceLink part.

ext.description: Your runtime's own fields for this part, carried through untouched.
